punchline: Leonardo da Vinci's notebooks look less like essays and more like Mind Maps.
thirty_sec: Leonardo da Vinci left thousands of notebook pages where sketches, diagrams, arrows and notes mix freely. Tony Buzan, creator of the Mind Map, saw them as evidence that great thinkers combine images, words and connections, unlike the linear, one-color notes most of us learned in school. His Mind Map was designed to give everyone a more visual, connected way to think on paper.
question: What do your notes usually look like?
key_contrast: Lines of text versus images and connections
